definitions.explanation: A series of large ocean waves typically caused by underwater earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or landslides, capable of causing devastating destruction in coastal areas.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{地震|じしん}の{後|あと}、{津波|つなみ}{警報|けいほう}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: A tsunami warning was issued after the large earthquake.

examples.japanese: {津波|つなみ}が{海岸|かいがん}の{町|まち}を{襲|おそ}った。
examples.english: The tsunami hit the coastal town.

examples.japanese: {津波|つなみ}が{来|く}たら{高台|たかだい}に{避難|ひなん}してください。
examples.english: If a tsunami comes, please evacuate to higher ground.

notes:
The Japanese word {津波|つなみ} has been adopted internationally as the standard term for this phenomenon. The kanji literally mean "harbor wave" ({津|つ} = harbor, {波|なみ} = wave).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {津波|つなみ}{警報|けいほう} (tsunami warning)
- {津波|つなみ}{注意報|ちゅういほう} (tsunami advisory)
- {津波|つなみ}が{来|く}る (a tsunami is coming)
- {津波|つなみ}に{襲|おそ}われる (to be hit by a tsunami)
- {津波|つなみ}{避難|ひなん} (tsunami evacuation)

RELATED TERMS:
- {地震|じしん} (earthquake)
- {高台|たかだい} (high ground)
- {避難|ひなん} (evacuation)
